newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile police search for leader of secretive colony.
newsitem.headline: Chile police search for leader of secretive colony.

text.p: A Chilean official said on Tuesday authorities believe a fugitive leader of a secretive German colony in southern Chile was being hidden by friends, and that they could be held criminally liable as accomplices.
Paul Schaeffer, a German immigrant who founded the Colonia Dignidad (Dignity Colony) settlement, is wanted on charges of child abuse, said Deputy Interior Minister Belisario Velasco.
Some news reports have said Schaeffer may have left the country, but Velasco said authorities now believed he was somewhere in Chile, hiding out with the help of friends.

Schaeffer is the leader of the insular, German-speaking colony in the Andean foothills whose members have been accused of abusing and illegally imprisoning children. A Chilean judge issued an arrest warrant for Schaeffer late last year on charges of molesting boys.
"We want Mr. Schaeffer to turn himself in to the courts to answer the abuse charges that on more than one occasion have been made against him," Velasco said.

"Unfortunately, the police have not been able to find him, and that being the case, there is not only one person committing a crime but also those who are his accomplices or hiding him," Velasco told reporters.
Velasco's words amounted to a warning to the colony's members, said to number a few hundred, that they could be held criminally liable if Schaeffer were found among them.

The colony was founded in the 1960s at the foot of the Andes near the town of Parral. Human rights groups have charged the colony was used as a detention centre in the 1970s for political prisoners during General Augusto Pinochet's military rule.
